# openinfra_training_job (Resource)

A run-once, GPU-capable model-training job (SageMaker Training Jobs) — runs a training container to completion, reading a dataset and writing artifacts to the object store. The training counterpart to openinfra_model (inference).



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `image` (String) Training container image. It runs to completion; write artifacts to the output bucket.
- `name` (String) Resource name. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `args` (List of String) Optional container args.
- `backoff_limit` (Number) How many times the Job retries a failed pod before it is marked Failed.
- `command` (List of String) Optional entrypoint override (container command).
- `cpu` (String) CPU request/limit as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g. `2`).
- `dataset` (Attributes) Input data location in the object store (injected as DATASET_BUCKET/DATASET_PREFIX + S3 creds). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dataset))
- `env` (Attributes List) Environment variables — the place to pass hyperparameters and config. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--env))
- `gpu` (Number) GPUs to request. `0` runs CPU-only; >0 schedules on a GPU node.
- `gpu_tier` (String) GPU class when gpu>0. One of: `smallgpu` (A2000 class), `largegpu` (e.g. 3090).
- `max_runtime_seconds` (Number) Hard wall-clock cap (Job activeDeadlineSeconds). Unset means no cap.
- `memory` (String) Memory request/limit as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g. `8Gi`).
- `namespace` (String) Kubernetes namespace. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `output` (Attributes) Where the job writes artifacts (injected as OUTPUT_BUCKET/OUTPUT_PREFIX + S3 creds). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--output))
- `secrets` (List of String) Extra secrets to inject with envFrom (e.g. a registry or HF token).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `namespace/name`, the import identifier.
- `job_name` (String) The batch Job the run executes as.
- `ready` (Boolean) Whether the resource's Ready condition is True. Terraform returns as soon as the object is accepted, so this is usually `false` immediately after apply — the platform reconciles asynchronously.
